subject: Re: CAIQ control annotation + executive summary for Aureum Analytics
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Mercer <t.mercer@aureum.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T08:02:00Z
Subject: CAIQ control annotation + executive summary for Aureum Analytics

Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. As discussed, attached is our initial CAIQ crosswalk where we’ve annotated Redwood’s mappings to the CSA controls (column: Redwood interpretation). It’s intentionally opinionated — our goal is to give Aureum a concise artifact you can hand to your InfoSec reviewers rather than the full policy dump.

What you’ll find in the attached workbook:
- Tab A: control-by-control mapping (high level mapping + pointer to evidence)
- Tab B: evidence index (log ranges, retention windows, sample artifact names)
- Tab C: open clarifying questions we flagged for you

Quick asks:
1) Could you confirm whether you want the mapping to reference the production VPC or the sandbox environment? We defaulted to production.
2) Any controls you want expanded into narrative form for execs? We can produce a one-page executive summary per control category.

I’ve cc’d Grace (security ops) to coordinate the artifact shipment window. We’ll prepare an executive summary doc once you confirm the target scope (production vs sandbox) and any redlines.

Attachments: CAIQ_initial_crosswalk.xlsx (workbook; annotated mapping)

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Mercer <t.mercer@aureum.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aureum Security <security@aureum.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T10:18:00Z
Subject: Re: CAIQ control annotation + executive summary for Aureum Analytics

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the annotated workbook. A few notes after our initial pass:

- Scope: please keep everything scoped to production. Audit reviewers will want production telemetry and the service-level VPC.
- Evidence ask: we need log retention proof for the 30-day and 90-day windows (details in Aureum_control_questions.pdf attached). For a handful of controls (IaaS identity and key rotation), the auditor wants an example KMS rotation event and a sanitized key-policy snippet.
- Narrative: the external audit team would appreciate a two-page executive summary focused on data residency, retention guarantees, and fallback policies in cross-region outages.

We’ll attach a prioritized control list on our side; I included that as "Aureum_control_questions.pdf". Grace — can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a sanitized KMS rotation event and a redacted IAM policy? Those are must-haves for the auditor.

Tom
Tom Mercer
Head of Security, Aureum Analytics
t.mercer@aureum.ai | +1 646 555 0123

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Mercer <t.mercer@aureum.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: CAIQ control annotation + executive summary for Aureum Analytics

Tom / Jordan —

Quick legal/security note from our side: we can provide a sanitized KMS rotation event (redacted key IDs, timestamps preserved) and a redacted IAM policy that demonstrates role bindings and least privilege — both as PDF export stubs. Expected delivery: by EOD Wednesday (2027-10-06).

Log retention proof: we can export retention configuration screenshots and a sample aggregated log bundle (sanitized) that shows retention metadata for 30/90 day indices. We will not include any customer PII in the samples; Grace will coordinate the sanitization.

On the executive summary: Jordan / Grace — I recommend the summary call out three items explicitly for Aureum auditors:
- Data residency commitments (regions and storage location)
- Retention and access review cadence (who signs off and how often)
- Outage fallback and failover policy plus verification evidence (runbook excerpt)

Tom — if you can send the auditor contact (name + email) we can include them on a delivery email and add a short DOA (description of attachments) that auditors prefer.

Attachments (to be delivered): evidence_links_manifest.csv (manifest with Drive links + short descriptions)

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Mercer <t.mercer@aureum.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T16:12:00Z
Subject: Fwd: CAIQ control annotation + executive summary delivery — Aureum Analytics

Tom —

Per Kim’s note, we’ve packaged the artifacts and the two-page executive summary you requested. See the Drive bundle link in the manifest (attached). Summary of what’s in the package:

1) Redwood_CAIQ_ExecSummary_v1.docx — two pages covering data residency, retention guarantees, and cross-region fallback policy (written for auditors and execs).
2) CAIQ_initial_crosswalk.xlsx — annotated control mapping (finalized with minor clarifications from Aureum_control_questions.pdf).
3) evidence_links_manifest.csv — Drive links and short descriptions for each artifact (KMS rotation export, sanitized IAM policy PDF, retention screenshots, aggregated log bundle sample).

For auditors: the Drive bundle contains read-only copies and an expiring link. If the auditors require a signed attestation, let us know and we’ll escalate to the compliance team for an attestation letter.

Next steps / asks:
- Tom: confirm the auditor contact and whether you want the sanitized artifacts delivered directly to them or via your team.
- Kim: can you confirm we’re ok to add a one-line attestation placeholder in the exec summary for now ("attestation available on request") until legal final sign-off?

Thanks — we’ll stand by for the auditor contact and any redlines.

Attachments: Redwood_CAIQ_ExecSummary_v1.docx; evidence_links_manifest.csv; CAIQ_initial_crosswalk.xlsx

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
